steps.title: Same query, every time
steps.caption: Every dashboard view re-runs the same join and aggregation on the source tables: slow, every time.
steps.body: The dashboard asks one question: revenue per product. Against the source tables that is a join of `order_items` with `products` and an aggregation over every order line, and it runs again for every viewer, even when almost nothing has changed since the last run. It is slow (1.8 s here, an illustrative figure), and it competes with the transactions that write those same tables.

steps.title: Precompute the answer
steps.caption: A materialized view stores the answer, one row per product; the dashboard just reads rows in 5 ms.
steps.body: A **materialized view** stores the result of that query in the shape the question needs: one row per product, complete for every product and computed before anyone asks. The dashboard now reads a few rows by key (5 ms here, also illustrative) and no longer touches the source tables. The view is **derived data**: it holds nothing that cannot be rebuilt from the source.

steps.title: Keep it fresh
steps.caption: A new order makes the view stale until a scheduled full refresh or an incremental update catches up.
steps.body: An order for two Mugs commits in the source, and the view is **stale** until it is refreshed, which its as-of time shows. A **scheduled full refresh** re-runs the whole query every 15 minutes: simple, and stale for up to the interval. **Incremental maintenance** applies only the change (+2 units and +$40 on one row), driven by the stream of changes: fresher, at the price of more machinery.

steps.title: Rebuild it, know the price
steps.caption: For a new question, build a second view beside the first, switch readers, then drop the old one.
steps.body: The question changes to revenue per product *and region*, which the stored rows cannot answer. A new version of the view is built beside the old one from the source, readers switch once it is complete, and the old one is dropped. Every view has a price: storage, work on each write or refresh, answers that can be slightly behind and one more thing to operate, so materialize only queries that are both expensive and frequent.
